tasks.title: Confirm business details, NAICS codes, and Keeper access
tasks.instructions: Start here before filling in vendor applications. Review P-018 in CEO_Journal.md and Texas_Comptroller_Registration_Info.md in the Texas AI Consulting knowledge files. Confirm the legal business name, business address, contact email, approved W-9, service description, and primary/secondary NAICS codes with Elliott. The NIGP commodity codes in the Comptroller record are different from NAICS codes; do not substitute one for the other. Locate existing portal records in Keeper before creating any accounts. Use the authorized Texas AI Consulting shared folder and individual delegated access where the portal supports it. For every business login created or updated this week, save the correct portal URL, username, password, and recovery details in Keeper immediately. Keep passwords, tax IDs, and personal veteran documents out of task notes. Done when the verified business details and document locations are ready and Keeper access is confirmed; note only the readiness status and any missing items here.

tasks.title: Priority: add or complete the Bexar County supplier profile
tasks.instructions: Make Bexar County the first agency you work on after confirming the business details. Elliott met with Jason from Bexar County. Open the official Supplier Portal/Vendor Registration page and check Keeper and the portal for an existing Texas AI Consulting supplier account. Recover or finish that profile if it exists; otherwise register the business using the verified business details, W-9, accurate service/commodity categories, and notification email. The October conference attendee registration is separate and does not establish a supplier profile. Save all new or updated credentials in Keeper. Done when the supplier profile is submitted or an existing active profile is verified. Record the actual status, a non-sensitive confirmation/reference, and the next follow-up date. Pending review is not active approval; leave this task open if required documents or access prevent submission.

Save authorized business login details in Keeper, and keep personal identity and disability documents in their approved secure location. Done when the prior status and next-step checklist are verified with Elliott; put only a brief non-sensitive summary and secure document location in the task note. If the status cannot be verified, leave the task open and record the blocker.

Run searches for AI automation, AI chatbot, GoHighLevel, and GHL; check both AI and GHL opportunities each day. Review scope, budget, client history, timing, and fit with Texas AI Consulting's actual capabilities. Save up to three strong matches and add their job links plus a one-line fit/risk summary in the completion note. If none fit, record that both categories were checked and no suitable jobs were found. This task covers research and shortlisting; flag proposal candidates to Elliott without spending Connects or submitting proposals as part of this check. Keep authorized business credentials in Keeper.

tasks.title: Verify or complete the SAM.gov entity registration
tasks.instructions: Check for Texas AI Consulting's existing entity and UEI before starting anything new. Verify whether the entity has an active registration for federal contracting, not just a UEI. Use the existing entity administrator or request the appropriate delegated role; work with Elliott on owner-only steps. If no registration exists, prepare and complete the correct registration using the verified legal information, NAICS codes, and required records. If an existing registration needs renewal or correction, address that record instead of creating a duplicate. Have Elliott confirm any business representations that require his certification. SAM.gov registration is free. Save authorized login details in Keeper. Done when active status is verified or the completed registration/update has been submitted; record the actual status, renewal/follow-up date, and any dependency for SBA VetCert. If you cannot submit because information or owner action is missing, leave the task open with the blocker.

tasks.title: Assess GSA Schedule eligibility and application requirements
tasks.instructions: Timebox the initial GSA Multiple Award Schedule review to about 45 minutes. Identify the service categories/SINs that fit Texas AI Consulting, required experience and financial/past-performance records, mandatory preparation, and current application steps. Compare those requirements with our actual records. If a standard requirement is missing, check whether an official alternative such as Startup Springboard could apply rather than assuming eligibility. Note SAM dependencies and the effort needed for an offer. Done when a short fit/gap checklist and a recommended next action are saved in the task note or linked working document. This is an eligibility assessment, not a GSA contract award or a promise to submit an entire offer this week. If account access is needed, check existing records first and store authorized credentials in Keeper.

tasks.instructions: Review TxDOT's official supplier guidance for the AI, software, automation, and consulting services we actually offer. The linked goods/non-professional-services guidance starts with CMBL, so use Tuesday's verified listing and check the relevant NIGP categories and ESBD opportunities. Confirm which procurement route applies to our offerings; do not create a construction-contractor account merely to tick a box. Check whether an additional TxDOT supplier profile or system registration is required for the relevant route, then verify an existing account or complete the required profile if applicable. Save any credentials in Keeper. Done when the applicable route, current registration coverage, and any additional steps are documented. If the route requires no separate registration, say that explicitly with the official source; otherwise record the submitted/current status or leave the task open if required registration is blocked.

tasks.title: Assess DIR opportunities and the vendor or partner route
tasks.instructions: Timebox the first DIR review to about 45 minutes. Identify current or upcoming solicitations that fit Texas AI Consulting's real IT/AI services. Record the relevant solicitation links, deadlines, qualifications, and submission system, if any. DIR prime vendor status requires the applicable solicitation and contract process; creating a portal login alone is not an award. If no suitable prime opportunity is open, identify up to two relevant existing DIR contract holders as possible subcontract/reseller partners and document the route for Elliott to consider. Done when the fit, requirements, and next action are documented, including 'no suitable current solicitation' if that is the finding. Save any authorized portal credentials in Keeper.

tasks.title: Review TXMAS eligibility before attempting an application
tasks.instructions: Review the current official TXMAS eligibility page against Texas AI Consulting's actual offerings. The published scope excludes information technology and consulting services and requires a qualifying existing government contract. Check those exclusions first. If our offerings are outside TXMAS scope, record 'not applicable for the reviewed offerings' with the reason and identify DIR or another relevant route as the next step. Only if an actual offering qualifies, list the required base contract, documents, submission window, and remaining gaps for Elliott. Done when the eligibility finding and source are documented. Do not submit an unsupported application or describe this review as a TXMAS registration. Save any necessary authorized account credentials in Keeper.

Review current proposal categories against our actual AI, software, automation, and consulting offerings.
